doc.title: Akiyoshi Toshiko — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Renting rooms in Tokyo
summary: Where she lived in Tokyo: rooms rented from families who lost income after the war.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: [Laughs] Let‟s go back to when you first got to Tokyo, um, about your impressions of Tokyo, and where you first stayed. Did you have any con … you had this letter of introduction,
…but did you have a place to stay? How did you, what was your social situation?
My mother‟s friend was quite wealthy, they had a house in Setagaya, and uh….
Setagaya, which is like, uh … here it would be, say, oh….
Well, I have a map of Tokyo, would it be…?
Yes, Setagaya-ku [ward], yes. Setagaya-ku is a more residential area. They have a densha [train] from Shibuya station to, on the way to Yokohama.

They had a house, so I had one room upstairs they rented to me. So, those days … later, yeah, I also left there and went to other places. But it‟s always, those days I was always renting one room or the upstairs. Later on, before, maybe a year before I came to this country, I was in Shinagawa, and upstairs.… See, in those days, after the war was ended, many, relatively wealthy people lost income, so they rented out rooms for the income. So there was quite a lot of those, y‟know. And, uh, the last one I had, they converted so there was a kitchen upstairs, and things like that.
So you actually didn‟t have a piano in your house where you lived.
